If $D$ is the finite region enclosed by the curves $x=\frac{1}{4}(16-{y}^{2}),\,$ $x=4-y,$ and the line $y=1,$ as shown above, then ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA=$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's represent $D$ as a type II region. To determine the left and right functions, we draw a horizontal arrow from left to right through the region, as usual.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14154225/assets/e18c6c41d8fb3ffd15bd31741c849094055dbe3090c524e7645ba6463672d23d.png)

As a result, we get

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le 4,\,4-y\le x\le \frac{1}{4}(16-{y}^{2})\}.
$$

Therefore, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{4-y}^{(16-{y}^{2})/4}f(x,y)\,dx\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}[{\int }_{4-y}^{(16-{y}^{2})/4}f(x,y)\,dx]dy\end{aligned}
$$
